purpose: Automate git, branch, repository, disk/workspace, Kubernetes workload, and documentation-sprawl hygiene for the temporary GitHub lane-unlocker and native SCM/CI/CD cutover prep.

domains.policy: one isolated worktree branch per lane; no shared branch edits; branch owners record PR, disposition, and cleanup state
domains.automation: git worktree list --porcelain inventory plus future scm worktree lease registry; local static check is repo-hygiene-automation-check
domains.claim_boundary: does not delete worktrees or branches by default

domains.policy: short-lived branches, required GitHub lane-unlocker context, protected dev shadow config, squash/head-SHA pinning, and merge-queue/admission equivalence
domains.automation: GitHub Actions required check plus branch-protection shadow validation and future native SCM queue adapter tests
domains.claim_boundary: does not mutate live branch protection from local check

domains.policy: GitHub is temporary collaboration/publication bridge; native SCM owns durable commit graph and exposes GitHub public/private publication adapters
domains.automation: GitHub adapter contract tracks visibility, CODEOWNERS/rulesets, status publishing, PR mirror, and public/private split metadata
domains.claim_boundary: does not claim GitHub is permanent SCM

domains.policy: inventory-by-default for build artifacts, caches, temp files, and worktree residue; cleanup requires explicit safe flag or separate PR
domains.automation: specs/workspace-hygiene.json plus repo-hygiene-automation-check and future session-close inventory evidence
domains.claim_boundary: does not delete tracked files or external temp roots by default

domains.policy: controller-oriented scale-to-zero/pause/drain; never blind pod deletion; record namespace, workload kind/name, desired replicas, and rollback command
domains.automation: static policy now; future kubectl dry-run/inventory job and native cloud workspace controller action
domains.claim_boundary: does not scale or delete live Kubernetes workloads from local check

domains.policy: root docs stay pointer-thin; new docs are rejected unless registered, lane-owned, or archived; stale docs older than 3 days on GitHub are audit candidates
domains.automation: root markdown allowlist, root-hub pointer validation, doc-catalog stale marker, retired substrate tombstone registry, and future doc archive planner
domains.claim_boundary: does not bulk-delete historical ADRs or archives without evidence-backed migration

documentation_sprawl.shared_surface_rule: Shared docs/indexes/registries should point to disjoint lane-owned shards instead of becoming large mutable collaboration surfaces.
automation_targets: rust-buck2 stale documentation inventory test target
documentation_sprawl.retired_exact_name_scan: active root/canonical docs and specs must use the generic retired external SCM/CI/CD substrates term; exact names are allowed only in retired registry or historical ADR slug provenance.

stale_doc_inventory.source: git history in full-fetch GitHub/worktree contexts
stale_doc_inventory.implementation: tools/doc-staleness-inventory-app (Rust, Buck2-owned; optional local Cargo manifest is advisory only)

native_scm_adapter_contract.scm_core: pure-Rust Sapling-inspired Oyatie SCM owns durable commit graph, stacked changes, workspace leases, branch/merge state, and policy evaluation

github_public_private_publication_adapte.role: publish/mirror selected public and private repos, PRs, checks, releases, CODEOWNERS/rulesets, and statuses to GitHub while native SCM remains authoritative
github_public_private_publication_adapte.private_source_policy: private-by-default unless an explicit release/publication manifest selects public export
github_public_private_publication_adapte.public_source_policy: public mirrors are generated/published from native SCM export manifests; do not hand-edit divergent public repositories

git_protocol_adapter.role: interoperate with ordinary git clients, GitHub remotes, and emergency plain-git workflows

github_actions_status_bridge.role: consume/post temporary GitHub Actions statuses until native Oya CI is trusted

security_backlog_validation.source: user-requested zero-trust, CI/CD, data, IAM, and Kubernetes runtime hardening backlog review
security_backlog_validation.decision: All requested controls are valid as P00/P01 backlog items because they map to cloud-native or hyperscaler-grade least-privilege, blast-radius, runtime-isolation, data-protection, and supply-chain patterns. They remain planning/backlog entries only and authorize no live Kubernetes, cloud, CI secret, branch-protection, or data-retention mutation.
security_backlog_validation.validity_rule: Keep a requested control when it reduces tenant/workload blast radius, removes implicit trust, strengthens provenance, or hardens runtime/data planes and has an official/upstream reference or hyperscaler-compatible pattern.
sequencing_notes: P00 defaults should cover CI secrets, restricted pod standards, dropped capabilities, default-deny NetworkPolicy intent, disabled service-account automounts, and workload identity design seams because they reduce immediate parallel-lane blast radius.

P01/P02 items such as service mesh mTLS, sandboxed/hardware-enforced isolation, host-based microsegmentation, and separate control planes require capacity, latency, operational complexity, and trust-tier tradeoff review before becoming universal defaults.
SCP-like guardrails are adopted as an Oyatie Cloud multi-account/project pattern, not as an AWS dependency claim.

security_hardening_backlog.backlog_action: Model service-to-service and user-to-resource access as continuous, policy-evaluated trust decisions; bind to Cloud IdP and admission policy.
Add just-in-time privileged elevation, approval, expiry, and audit for break-glass/admin access.
Design Cedar/OPA-style attribute policy for tenant/account/project/resource context beyond static RBAC roles.
Default-deny east-west traffic and allow only explicit service-to-service paths.
Separate integration surfaces per tenant/account/project and prevent shared integration credentials across silos.
Scope agent/automation identities, tools, memories, and data access per tenant/project/workload lane.
Encrypt sensitive data in transit and at rest, including Kubernetes API data and service-owned stores.
Add retention/deletion workflows for obsolete data discovered by hygiene inventories.
Rate-limit data-layer APIs and high-cardinality queries per tenant/workload to contain abuse and runaway agents.
Add session revocation hooks for risk events, privilege expiry, tenant disablement, and credential rotation.
Log both human principal and automation/agent/workload delegate for every privileged action.
Isolate CI lanes by repo/tenant/trust tier and prevent untrusted PR jobs from sharing privileged runners or secrets.
Use least-privilege GitHub permissions/OIDC and avoid long-lived broad secrets in workflows.
Pin action/tool/dependency versions and prefer private/controlled registries plus provenance where supported.
Deploy scoped honeytokens and instant alerts for credential misuse and unexpected data path access.
Evaluate host/workload firewalling and eBPF enforcement where Kubernetes NetworkPolicy is insufficient.
Use hardware-enforced isolation for high-risk workloads through confidential compute/sandbox runtimes where justified.
Model Oyatie Cloud org/account/project separation with account-level blast-radius boundaries.
Adopt SCP-like deny guardrails for Oyatie Cloud accounts/projects and native control planes.
Bind workloads to short-lived identities rather than static node/runner credentials.
Block pod access to cloud node metadata endpoints unless explicitly required by workload identity design.
Assign high-risk pods to isolated runtime classes and security profiles.
Enforce restricted pod standards: no privileged containers, no privilege escalation, limited host namespaces/paths.
Default service containers to read-only root filesystems with explicit writable volumes.
Drop all Linux capabilities by default and add only required capabilities per workload exception.
Require namespace default-deny ingress/egress policies before enabling service lanes.
Use service mesh mTLS for workload-to-workload identity and transport encryption where mesh overhead is justified.
Disable automatic service-account token mounts by default and opt in per workload.
Define cell/region/tenant blast walls across namespaces, node pools, clusters, and accounts.
Separate management/control planes from tenant workloads and high-risk experimentation lanes.
Adopt sandboxed runtimes through RuntimeClass for untrusted or high-risk workloads.
